Run End-to-end pipeline: ```bashpython scripts/run_all.py``` Produces every table and figure under `experiments/results/`. On a singleRTX 4090 the full run (5 seeds for CD-STHGT, 3 seeds for the ten baselines,200 epochs) finishes in roughly 11 hours. Stage-by-stage: ```bash# CD-STHGT, five seeds, 200 epochspython scripts/train_cdsthgt.py \ --config configs/cdsthgt.yaml \ --output experiments/results/cdsthgt_table7.json # Ten baselines, three seeds, 50 epochs eachpython scripts/train_baselines.py \ --config configs/cdsthgt.yaml \ --epochs 50 --seeds 0 1 2 \ --baselines ARIMA XGBoost LSTM Informer iTransformer \ STGCN GraphWaveNet HGT CaST DVGNN \ --output experiments/results/baselines_table7.json # Tables 7 through 14python scripts/aggregate_results.py # CD-Shapley attribution at the 2020 forecast originpython scripts/run_attribution.py --origin 2020 --n_permutations 64 # Figures 3 and 7 through 14python scripts/generate_figures.py``` --- ## Project structure ```cdsthgt/├── README.md (this file)├── requirements.txt├── LICENSE├── configs/│ └── cdsthgt.yaml Model and training hyperparameters├── data/ Place dataset here (see Section 2)├── src/│ ├── data/ Panel loader, dual-timescale graph│ │ builder, policy mediator,│ │ rolling-origin protocol│ ├── models/│ │ ├── cdsthgt.py CD-STHGT main model│ │ ├── dthg_module.py Meta-path attention,│ │ │ cycle-aware gated fusion│ │ ├── disentangle.py Ternary disentanglement,│ │ │ back-door and front-door adjustment│ │ └── baselines/│ │ └── all_baselines.py Ten baselines│ ├── attribution/│ │ └── cd_shapley.py Counterfactual Shapley│ ├── evaluation/│ │ └── metrics.py Evaluation metrics│ └── utils/│ └── seed.py Reproducibility helpers├── scripts/│ ├── train_cdsthgt.py Train the main model│ ├── train_baselines.py Train the ten baselines│ ├── aggregate_results.py Reproduce Tables 7 through 14│ ├── run_attribution.py CD-Shapley attribution│ ├── generate_figures.py Reproduce Figures 3, 7 through 14│ └── run_all.py Full end-to-end pipeline└── results/ ├── tables/ Reference tables (CSV) └── figures/ Reference figures (PNG)``` --- ## Dataset Full specification in `cdsthgt-dataset/README.md`. Summary: - 31 provincial administrative regions, 5 high-technology subindustries, 19 years (2005 through 2023) - 2,945 node-year observations.- 14 input features over five dimensions (innovation input, innovation output, innovation collaboration, economic environment, digital foundation) plus the composite innovation capability score on a 4.2 through 100 scale.- Five heterogeneous graph relations (geographic adjacency, industrial-chain coupling, technological similarity, talent mobility, patent citation), the slow ones as yearly weighted adjacency matrices and the fast ones as dated quarterly events.- 326 central-government policy documents with LDA topic intensities and topic-subindustry similarities.- Supplementary materials: IPC-to-subindustry concordance, inventor disambiguation dictionary, recruitment-platform flow panel, keyword dictionary, stopword list, three central-government policy events, provincial centroid coordinates and contiguity pairs. Primary sources: *China High-Technology Industry Statistical Yearbook*,*China Science and Technology Statistical Yearbook*, *China IndustrialStatistical Yearbook*, the CNIPA patent database, the *White Paper onChina's Digital Economy* of the China Academy of Information andCommunications Technology, and the State Council / MIIT / NDRC / MOSTpolicy archives. --- ## Model architecture ### Dual-timescale heterogeneous graph Transformer Meta-path aware multi-head attention over seven meta-paths plus twocomposite paths (Equation 2 of the paper). The cycle-aware gated fusion(Equation 3) uses a node-wise gate g[v, t] computed from the slow and fastweighted degree of v combined with the annual topic-intensity embedding. ```alpha[u, v, r, k] = softmax_u( ( W_Q^{r,k} h_v )^T ( W_K^{r,k} h_u ) / sqrt(d_k) * mu[r, k] )g[v, t] = sigmoid( w_g^T [ s^slow[v] s^fast[v] p[t] ] + b_g )A_slow^fuse[t] = diag(g[t]) * A^slow[t]A_fast^fuse[t] = diag(1 - g[t]) * A^fast[t]``` ### Ternary causal disentanglement Each node embedding h is projected to: - **z^c** = Encoder_c(h), the causal factor- **z^e** = Quantizer(h), the environmental factor on a 16-entry codebook- **z^s** = Encoder_s(h), the style factor An HSIC term enforces independence between z^c and z^e. The front-door andback-door adjustment (Equations 5 and 6) produces the causal prediction`P_causal = eta * P_back + (1 - eta) * P_front` with eta = 0.5. ### Causal trajectory rollout A gated recurrent cell rolls z^c forward one step at a time; the adjustmentreads out a prediction at each step. The composite loss is ```L = L_pred + 0.3 * L_traj + 0.01 * L_HSIC + 0.1 * L_rec``` where L_traj penalises the squared difference of successive z^c states. ### CD-Shapley attribution Permutation sampling with do-interventions on each feature; the baseline isthe zero vector in standardized feature space (the training-period mean).The time-dependent effect curve Phi_i(t) is produced by rollingone-feature-at-a-time counterfactuals through the input window. --- ## Reproducibility Random seeds are controlled by `src/utils/seed.py` and set under`training.seeds` in the YAML configuration. Standard deviations reported inthe paper's Table 7 come from the five seeds in the default configuration. Rolling-origin protocol (same as the paper): three forecast origins(2018, 2019, 2020), four horizons (1, 3, 5, 7 years), input window ofT = 5 years, slow-graph window of 3 years, fast-graph quarter window of 1,diffusion coefficient beta = 0.5.

title: How AI is transforming the way organizations think and learn
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Knowledge management is crucial in any firm and shaped by the different dimensions of organizational cognition. The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) broadens the scope for effective knowledge management strategies, but leaders must be aware of the need to ensure that the AI-human mechanisms used to develop strategies are utilized appropriately so that hybrid cognition proves effective. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

title: Quantum prepare-and-measure scenarios: concepts and methods
abstract: Prepare-and-measure scenarios are among the simplest and most widely used settings for quantum communication. A sender prepares a physical system in one of several possible states, which a receiver then measures. Despite this simple structure, these scenarios offer a rich framework for exploring the differences between classical and quantum communication, revealing quantum advantages, and developing protocols for quantum cryptography and device certification. In this tutorial, we give a ground-up introduction to prepare-and-measure scenarios and the methods used to study them. We introduce different frameworks for constraining and characterising communication, with an emphasis on semi-device-independent approaches to quantum information. We also cover modern convex-optimisation techniques for characterising the correlations achievable in these scenarios and illustrate how these tools can be applied in practice. Our aim is to give newcomers the conceptual and technical foundations needed to approach the current literature and apply prepare-and-measure methods in their own research. We conclude with a discussion of open problems and directions for future work.

title: Testing Conditional Distribution Equality Using Generative Models
abstract: Conditional distribution equality testing is a core problem with applications in causal inference, model diagnostics, and transfer learning. Existing methods often lose power when the conditioning variable is high-dimensional. We propose a new test that leverages generative models to compare conditional distributions using both observed data and synthetic samples. A sample-splitting and studentization scheme is introduced to control estimation error. Under the null, the test statistic is asymptotically normal, and we establish local power against contiguous alternatives. Our theory under the null and fixed alternative requires only consistency of the learned conditional distribution, allowing for a broad class of generative models. Empirical results demonstrate accurate size control and strong power in high-dimensional settings compared to representative kernel-based conditional and joint two-sample tests.

title: Photon Demultiplexing Using Spatial Routing
abstract: Spatial sectioning of the far-field noncollinear field from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is a promising approach for multiparty quantum communication. Although demonstrations with six pairs of users have been reported, the fundamental limits remain unknown. These include the maximum number of channels, the required degree of channel optimization, and the dependence on input parameters. In this paper, we provide a practical framework that answers these questions by connecting input parameters and invoking a design theorem. For a representative configuration, we realize 12 user-pair channels with routing consistency exceeding $0.9999$ at a $12\%$ reduction in photon flux. We further show that sectioning improves the accidental-coincidence budget linearly with the number of channels $N$, allowing the aggregate key rate to scale with the user count. These results provide a design strategy for spatial-division multiplexing of entangled photons analogous to the channel-spacing standards used in wavelength-division networks.

title: On the Limits of Representation-Based Test-Time Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Vision-language models suffer significant accuracy drops under common corruptions. While test-time adaptation (TTA) successfully mitigates these shifts in CLIP-like contrastive models, its application to generative multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains underexplored and uniquely challenging due to their sequential token generation. In this work, we demonstrate that representation-based TTA fails to recover performance in MLLMs. Our experiments reveal that even when violating standard TTA assumptions by leveraging target data offline, sample-blind feature alignment recovers only marginal accuracy. We attribute this failure to the nature of corruption shifts: unlike CLIP-like architectures, which benefit from a shared domain-shift direction within a single pooled classification embedding, MLLM visual token sequence shifts are nearly orthogonal and span the full embedding space.These findings bound what any sample-blind, position-shared correction at a single encoder site can achieve, establishing that representation-space interventions alone might be insufficient to ensure corruption robustness in MLLMs.

title: Annealed Lévy Diffusion via Gaussian Surrogate Reverse Dynamics
abstract: Gaussian diffusion models offer a practical framework for generative modeling. Denoising Lévy Probabilistic Models (DLPM) introduce heavy-tailed perturbations with a fixed tail index throughout denoising. We introduce Annealed Lévy Diffusion (ALD). ALD varies the stability index $α(t)$ to combine heavy-tailed exploration with Gaussian refinement. Our marginal-first formulation represents stable noise as a scalar Gaussian scale mixture. This formulation enables standard Gaussian noise-prediction training with one additional scale input. We study two sampling processes. ALD-renoise estimates the clean sample and injects fresh marginal noise. ALD-posterior preserves dependence between successive states through an accumulated conditional variance and a Gaussian bridge update. Both samplers reuse the same trained predictor with different scalar inputs. We evaluate ALD on four 2D benchmarks and an imbalanced nine-mode mixture. We also examine training efficiency and the effects of prediction perturbations on clipped Holtsmark data. Additional experiments evaluate MNIST and CelebA64 generation and CIFAR-10LT augmentation. ALD preserves local geometry on the evaluated light-tailed and manifold-structured targets.

title: Balanced Defensive Fine-Tuning for Text-to-SQL on a Small Code Language Model: A Pre-Registered Measurement Report
abstract: Locally run small language models enable generating SQL from natural language without sending the database schema to third-party servers. However, a model fine-tuned only to "translate the question into SQL" can also translate destructive or unauthorized commands embedded in the prompt. In this report we measure, under a pre-registered protocol, the Balanced SFT method applied with QLoRA (nf4, r=16) on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct. In this method each training example is drawn from the attack set with probability α and from the legitimate Spider set with probability 1−α. The compared conditions are: the untrained base model (B0), standard SFT on legitimate data only (A0, α=0), balanced SFT (A.3, α=0.3), and SFT on defense data only (A1, α=1.0). Each trained condition was run with 3 seeds. The test sets consist of 500 attack prompts, 1034 Spider-dev questions, and 24 legitimate questions that contain risky words. Attack success rate (ASR) measured with a database-execution (DB-exec) judge is 61.53% ± 2.53 on A0 and 0.00% on A.3. The difference is −61.53 points, with 95% confidence interval [−64.73; −58.53]. Official test-suite execution accuracy (EX) is 70.25% ± 0.49 on A0 and 69.50% ± 0.88 on A.3. The difference is −0.74 points, with 95% confidence interval [−2.06; 0.55]. Thus H1 (security) and H2 (cost, non-inferiority) pass the pre-specified thresholds. However, the protocol-mandated human judge audit of 100 examples was not performed and will not be performed (Appendix A, S18). ASR was measured only with the automatic DB-exec judge; because judge validity was not tested against human labels, both hypotheses are reported only as supported (provisional), and this label can no longer become definitive. The over-refusal hypothesis H3 remains exploratory because the test set was reduced from 250 to 24: even with 0/24 errors the Wilson upper bound is 13.8% and lies above the 10% threshold. The α=1.0 condition collapsed on all three seeds to a solution that rejects every input. Deviations from the locked plan and unplanned analysis decisions are collected in a single table in Appendix A, with dates and whether they were taken before or after results were seen (11 coded deviations, 6 uncoded decisions; 17 items, 18 rows). Seven of these items were taken after results were seen. Among them are the 14 October 2026 finalization of the decision to stop at 3 seeds, the merging of the category 3/4 rule in the DB-exec judge, and moving the human-audit target from A.3_s11 to A0_s11. The collapse of A1 and the fact that ASR is a proxy measurement are not deviations but a result and a measurement note.

title: ropensci/ibger: ibger 0.2.1
abstract: The package was peer-reviewed and accepted by rOpenSci (ropensci/software-review#787). The repository moved to https://github.com/ropensci/ibger and the documentation to https://docs.ropensci.org/ibger/; the rOpenSci Code of Conduct now applies. Changes from the rOpenSci review (ropensci/software-review#787) Second review (@ddiannae) parse_sidra_url() / fetch_sidra_url(): a SIDRA URL without a /p/ (periods) segment no longer crashes the print method and the fetch; the equivalent call falls back to the ibge_variables() default (last 6 periods) (reported by @ddiannae). parse_sidra_url(): a territorial level that is not in the internal lookup table (e.g. n12) no longer errors with "subscript out of bounds". Levels that the aggregate does not offer now raise a warning at parse time listing the available levels, and fetch_sidra_url() fails through the regular validation (reported by @ddiannae). parse_sidra_url(): URLs with several territorial levels (e.g. n1/all/n3/all) produced an "Equivalent ibger call" with an unnamed list that ibge_variables() rejects. The printed call and fetch_sidra_url() now share one translation: a named list when every level has specific codes, and the API's pipe syntax ("N1|N3[33,35]") otherwise (reported by @ddiannae). ibge_aggregates() now checks the format of its five filters before the request. The API silently drops filters it cannot parse (returning the whole catalog under a success message) and answers HTTP 500 to others, e.g. periodicity = 30; malformed values now abort with an example of the expected format. An empty result is reported with a warning instead of a green "0 aggregates found", and keeps the documented columns (reported by @ddiannae). ibge_aggregates(): the periodicity codes in the documentation were wrong (P10 and P58 do not exist; P13 is the rolling quarter, not annual). The documented table now lists the codes observed in the catalog: P1 annual, P5 monthly, P8 semi-annual, P9 quarterly, P13 rolling quarter, plus the multi-year codes (reported by @ddiannae). ibge_localities() with several levels queries each level separately and binds the results: the API's own multi-level endpoint returns an empty list as soon as one of the levels has no localities for the aggregate. An empty result now keeps the documented columns and is reported with a warning (reported by @ddiannae). The "exceeds the 100,000 value limit" hint on HTTP 500 is now only shown for data requests (ibge_variables()); for the other endpoints, where a 500 means the API could not interpret the request (non-existent aggregate, invalid filter), the message says so (reported by @ddiannae). Vignettes: getting-started and api-concepts are now precomputed against the live API like the other two (vignettes/precompile.R), so every printed output is real. This removed a set of wrong hand-written outputs — aggregate 1705 (IPCA-15) was described as the quarterly animal slaughter table, which is 1092; the ibge_variables(1705, localities = "N3") example (also in ?ibge_variables) errors because 1705 has no state level; periodicity = "P10" returned nothing — and replaced the advice to split large queries by hand with a section on the automatic chunking (chunk) in all three vignettes that mentioned the limit (reported by @ddiannae; precomputing suggested by @beatrizmilz). ibge_localities() example: ibge_localities(1437, level = c("N6", "N7")) returned an empty tibble (1437 has no metropolitan-area localities); the example now uses c("N2", "N3") (reported by @ddiannae). First review (@allanvc) Fixed the bsicons availability check in ibge_explorer(), which told users to install bslib instead of bsicons (reported by @allanvc). Fixed the documentation of the launch.browser argument of ibge_explorer(), which described FALSE as the default; the default is and remains TRUE (open in the browser), and FALSE opens the app in the RStudio Viewer pane (reported by @allanvc). Documented the IBGE API's server-side latency for large queries in ?ibge_variables and the README: municipality-level requests can take one to several minutes each (suggested by @allanvc). README: replaced the link to IBGE's terms of use, whose old address now returns a 404, with the current "Termo de Uso e Política de Privacidade" page (reported by @allanvc). Removed the stray .Rhistory file from the repository (suggested by @allanvc). curl (>= 6.0.0) is now declared in Imports, enforcing at install time the version requirement that was previously only documented in the README (older curl versions fail with curl_modify_url is not an exported object). The table of IBGE special value codes (-, .., ..., X) is now documented in a single place — ?parse_ibge_value — and linked from the README and vignettes instead of being repeated. The ipca-example and tutorial vignettes are now precompiled from .Rmd.orig sources against the live IBGE API (vignettes/precompile.R), so their output and ggplot2 figures render on the pkgdown site. README: added the rOpenSci review badge, linked the API-concepts vignette from the quick start, pointed the "Value column" section to parse_ibge_value(), and rewrote the ibge_explorer() section to match the tone of the rest of the page. Examples no longer use \dontrun{}: examples that query the live IBGE API (or launch the Shiny explorer) are now guarded with @examplesIf interactive(), so they render in the docs and run for interactive users without hitting the network during checks. Internal refactor to address the remaining pkgcheck/goodpractice notes: every function is now below the cyclomatic-complexity threshold of 15 (long functions such as parse_sidra_url(), fetch_sidra_url(), ibge_metadata() and ibge_survey_metadata() were decomposed into focused helpers), duplicated @param docs were replaced with @inheritParams, and the lintr issues flagged in the review (long lines, expect_equal() vs expect_identical(), static regexes without fixed = TRUE, duplicate cli bullet names, <<-, require() in the Shiny app, setwd() in precompile.R) were cleaned up. No user-facing behavior changes. title: Patentability of artificial intelligence (AI) inventions: A comparative study of Section 3(k) of the Indian Patents Act, 1970 and the United Kingdom's journey from Aerotel to emotional perception AI
abstract: This article undertakes a comparative doctrinal analysis of the patentability of artificial-intelligence (AI)-related inventions under Indian and UK patent law. Between 2023 and early 2026, the Delhi High Court, in a series of decisions culminating in Kroll Information Assurance, LLC v Controller General of Patents , refined the ‘technical effect/technical contribution’ threshold that governs the exclusion of ‘a computer programme per se’ under Section 3(k) of the Patents Act, 1970. That threshold has since been codified, with AI-specific illustrations, in the Guidelines for Examination of Computer Related Inventions, 2025, issued on 29 July 2025. The United Kingdom's position developed less smoothly. In Emotional Perception AI Ltd v Comptroller-General of Patents , a permissive first-instance ruling was reversed by the Court of Appeal, which reaffirmed the primacy of the long-standing four-step Aerotel test, before the Supreme Court, on 11 February 2026, overruled Aerotel altogether and adopted an approach modelled on the European Patent Office's ‘any hardware’ doctrine. This article argues that, notwithstanding these divergent statutory architectures and procedural histories, India and the United Kingdom have arrived at a structurally similar solution: a low, largely formal threshold for patent eligibility, followed by a substantive technical–character enquiry applied at a later analytical stage.

title: Wavelet compression for sampling deep Gaussian processes
abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) use iterative sampling to create non-stationary random fields. This is notoriously expensive because the covariance at each non-initial layer depends on the realised field from the layer below, so it changes with every sample. Moreover, standard fast sampling techniques like circulant embedding or matrix compression fail since the underlying kernel usually lacks the necessary regularity and structure. We develop and analyse a wavelet compression method for convolution Matérn DGPs. At each layer the covariance matrix is compressed using wavelets and a Lanczos algorithm computes the random sample. For specific parameter ranges involving the smoothness of the Matérn kernel as well as the smoothness of the wavelets, we show that the accumulative compression and sampling errors through all layers decay exponentially with increasing truncation parameter. We obtain a practical DGP sampling algorithm by choosing a truncation that gives log-linear covariance storage and matrix-vector costs, enabling DGP sampling at nearly linear computational cost.

title: PPAD-Completeness of Contiguous Envy-Free Cake Cutting with Additive Valuations
abstract: We prove that computing a complete contiguous $\varepsilon$-envy-free cake allocation is PPAD-complete for normalized rational piecewise-constant additive valuations. The hardness holds even when $\varepsilon$ is given in unary, and even when every density takes only two values, which are the same for all agents, and is piecewise constant with at most six breakpoints. As a consequence, computing an exact contiguous envy-free allocation is also PPAD-complete, and the hardness holds under the same restrictions on the densities. Our key ingredient is to assign prices to the pieces so that, in every approximately envy-free allocation, all prices are nearly equal, regardless of how the pieces are assigned to the agents. We further show that, for every fixed integer $c\ge1$, computing a contiguous EF$c$ allocation of indivisible goods on a path is PPAD-complete for additive valuations, and the hardness holds even for binary valuations in which each good is valued by exactly one agent and all agents value the same number of goods.

title: AdCoEvo: A Co-Evolving Multi-Agent Advertising Delivery System
abstract: Digital advertising is an important means for platforms to reach potential users and drive business growth. Advertising delivery is the core link between marketing objectives and actual returns. Existing methods have achieved partial automation in individual tasks such as bidding and budget allocation, but they still rely on human operators for overall coordination, making it difficult to support large-scale operations. They also often fail to achieve optimal performance, and individual experience remains difficult to turn into reusable operational capabilities. In addition, as advertising markets change, advertising delivery systems need timely strategy updates to remain effective in dynamic markets. To automate the entire advertising operations process and improve adaptability to market changes, we propose AdCoEvo, a co-evolving multi-agent advertising delivery system. Specifically, the system connects delivery decisions across different timescales and operational granularities through role specialization. Diagnostic results guide account planning and strategy adjustment in the next period. The multi-agent system updates its model parameters based on actual delivery outcomes and continually improves delivery strategies through mutual feedback among planning, adjustment, and diagnosis, thereby achieving co-evolution. Experiments show that, relative to the rule-based operational baseline (Rule), AdCoEvo increases advertiser value by 14.02% while reducing cost per acquisition by 7.07%. Compared with a multi-agent system with fixed parameters, AdCoEvo increases advertiser value by 3.96% and reduces cost per acquisition by 1.24%, indicating that co-evolution can yield greater delivery returns.

title: Authorship Attribution in Arabic: Teaching Companion
abstract: This teaching companion accompanies Chapter 8, Authorship Attribution in Arabic: From Stylometric Methods to Large Language Models, prepared for the edited volume Arabic Digital Humanities (John Benjamins). It provides an illustrated teaching guide, Python and R scripts, fixed evaluation folds, corpus and excerpt manifests, recorded predictions, software information, and publication figures. The main exercise uses twelve narrative works by four modern Arabic authors. Burrows's Delta is calculated with the R package stylo using training-only feature selection and scaling; word and character TF-IDF representations feed linear support vector machines. Whole works are held out during evaluation. A separate stylo interface exercise explores similarity across all twelve sampled work profiles, with full dialogue screenshots, visible selection markers and a complete cluster plot. An optional local Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct exercise demonstrates prompted attribution. Its shorter passages and smaller reference budget require separate interpretation from the Delta and SVM results. Classroom activities connect errors and clustering to close reading and distinguish completed analyses from proposed extensions. The package preserves the recorded analyses from 14 October 2026 and provides verified rerun instructions. Raw source books, reconstructed passages and model weights are not redistributed; retrieval instructions and checksums identify the sources. Original teaching documentation and figures are licensed under CC BY 4.0; original scripts are licensed under MIT. Third-party materials retain their own terms, as detailed in LICENSE.md. Version 1.0.1 corrects caption layout by separating figure and screenshot titles from explanatory paragraphs. It restores author label colours in the complete cluster plot and retains monochrome PNG and vector PDF alternatives. The publication plotting script generates both variants. The underlying data, clustering and recorded evaluation results are unchanged.

title: Ethics-Aware Hybrid Graph–Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Adaptive Fraud Management in Large-Scale Financial Systems
abstract: Fraud management systems are becoming more and more based on data-driven artificial intelligence processes to identify anomalous and malicious behavior in massive digital ecosystems. Nevertheless, the current solutions are usually characterized by low flexibility, inability to be interpreted, and such ethical limitations like bias, biased decision-making, and low transparency. This paper aims to tackle these issues by introducing a hybrid ethics-aware framework of fraud management relying on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning, and Reinforcement Learning (RL) as one framework. The suggested model assumes transactional environments to be dynamic graphs, which allows GNNs to efficiently learn the relation pattern and identify coordinated fraudulent patterns that are challenging in conventional feature-based models. In order to increase transparency and ethical adherence, domain-specific rules, regulatory requirements and principles of fairness would be directly inserted into the decision maker with a neuro-symbolic reasoning layer. Moreover, the limited reinforcement learning subsystem is continuously refining the policies of fraud detection in response to changing fraud methods, and it optimizes the risk thresholds, being explicit about avoiding ethical risks such as discriminatory results and excessive false positives. Empirical studies of benchmark fraud data sets show that the hybrid framework proposed can much better detect fraud, be resistant to concept drift, and explain decisions compared to traditional machine learning and deep models. Moreover, it is stated that ethical performance indicators are more favorable, and the framework is appropriate to be applied in actual financial and digital security systems. The findings reveal the promise of ethics-based hybrid AI systems as a dependable and trustworthy solution to fraud management in the new generation.

title: Adaptive Switching between Autonomous and Collaborative Exploration for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Multiple large language models (LLMs) can explore complex problem spaces independently or collaboratively. Autonomous exploration allows each model to develop distinct hypotheses, investigate alternative solution paths, and reduce premature convergence caused by shared assumptions. Collaborative exploration enables models to exchange findings, identify complementary information, resolve disagreements, and construct solutions using distributed knowledge. However, consistently relying on either exploration mode may limit problem-solving effectiveness. Permanent autonomous exploration can produce redundant investigations and prevent useful knowledge exchange, whereas permanent collaborative exploration can encourage premature consensus, correlated errors, and the suppression of unconventional ideas. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Autonomous and Collaborative Exploration for Multiple Large Language Models (ASACE), a framework in which multiple LLM agents dynamically switch between independent exploration and collaborative exploration according to the evolving characteristics of the task. Rather than prescribing a fixed collaboration schedule, ASACE evaluates exploration progress, estimated information gain, inter-agent disagreement, search redundancy, solution quality, and computational cost to determine the appropriate exploration mode at each decision point. The framework incorporates autonomous exploration, selective knowledge exchange, collaborative exploration, outcome evaluation, and adaptive mode selection into a unified iterative process. A mode-selection mechanism is formulated to balance exploration diversity, collective learning, solution quality, and resource efficiency. The framework also introduces an optional hysteresis mechanism to reduce unstable switching between exploration modes. This paper formalizes the proposed framework, presents its algorithmic procedure, discusses implementation strategies, and develops an experimental protocol for evaluating its effectiveness. Comparisons with permanently autonomous, permanently collaborative, and fixed-schedule hybrid baselines are proposed across reasoning, mathematical problem-solving, software engineering, scientific discovery, and search tasks. The central hypothesis is that adaptive switching can improve the balance between independent discovery and collective knowledge utilization when task conditions vary over time. The paper provides a research framework and testable hypotheses rather than claiming experimentally established improvements. Its contribution is the explicit formulation of exploration-mode selection as a dynamic control problem for multi-LLM systems.

title: Design and implementation of an AI-enabled English teaching support system
abstract: Traditional English teaching system has some problems, such as insufficient semantic understanding, low efficiency of personalized recommendation and high real-time interaction delay. This paper proposes an adaptive English teaching system based on AI. The system adopts a six layer microservice architecture, integrating rule parsing and deep learning hybrid syntax analysis engine, dynamic knowledge graph (KG), and dual tower neural network recommendation model, combined with Flink event time processing and CUDA parallel computing to optimize end-to-end latency to 10ms level. Experiments show that the F1 value of the hybrid parsing engine on FCE (First Certificate in English) data set is 0.857, which is 57.8% higher than that of the baseline model. Dynamic KG realizes non-monotonic updating of edge weights through error pattern capture, and RMSE (root mean square error) decreases by 55.2%. The cold start hit rate of the recommended model of twin towers is 0.547, which is better than that of LightGCN. The system supports 5500 concurrent requests, the delay of p99 is less than 200ms, and the error rate of non-native speech recognition words is reduced to 9.8%. The research results provide an engineering solution for the high concurrency and low delay requirements of online English teaching scenarios.

title: Dimension-Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning
abstract: Tracking changing comparators is a central problem in online learning. For exp-concave losses, previous work established the $T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon $T$ and Euclidean path length $P_T$ for fixed dimension, while the optimal cost of dimension remained unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing a sharp $d^{1/3}$ curved dimension factor, improving the $d^{2/3}$ factor of recent switching and interval reductions [1, 2]. To achieve this improvement, we develop a proper, full-information learner on compact convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that adapts to the unknown path length and, under fixed dimension-independent diameter, gradient, and curvature parameters, guarantees $$\operatorname{Reg}_T(u_{1:T}) \le \widetilde{O}\left(d+\min\left\{d^{1/3}T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3},\sqrt{TP_T},T\right\}\right).$$ A matching lower bound on a diameter-one Euclidean ball establishes the minimax frontier up to logarithmic factors when $T\gtrsim d^2$, including the transition from the curved rate to larger path budgets. The lower bound already holds for losses that depend on only one coordinate per round, isolating an unavoidable cost of learning across directions. Our upper bound follows from square-root Gaussian KL control of comparator movement and a cancellation argument that pays for history restarts. The curved learner maintains $O(\log^2 T)$ Gaussian states, uses one gradient per round, and runs in time near-linear in $T$ under a Mahalanobis-projection oracle.

title: Maximum likelihood, neural networks and posterior mean for inferring fractional Brownian motion parameters
abstract: Fractional Brownian motion (fBM) is a model of anomalous diffusion parameterised by a Hurst exponent $H \in (0,1)$ and a generalised diffusion coefficient $D_H > 0$. We jointly estimate $H$ and $D_H$ using maximum likelihood (MLE) from density measurements with Poisson counting noise and single-particle trajectory with Gaussian localisation error. We show that one density measurement in time cannot infer both $H$ and $D_H$ and that several time points are needed, which matters most for inference precision. For trajectories, we show that a neural network trained with a squared error loss approximates the posterior mean of $H$, which can be computed exactly at negligible cost. Paired with the profile-likelihood estimate of $D_H$, the posterior mean has the lowest root mean squared error in both $H$ and $D_H$, except near $H=0$ and $H=1$ where MLE estimates $H$ better. In vesicle trajectories from two cell types, $H$ and $D_H$ form a continuum rather than distinct modes of motion. The posterior probability that each window within a track is subdiffusive or superdiffusive shows that $26\%$ of MRC5 fibroblast and $21\%$ of HeLa vesicle trajectories contain both subdiffusive and superdiffusive windows, against $2\%$ and $7\%$ expected from estimation uncertainty alone. Intracellular cargoes therefore switch between subdiffusion and superdiffusion over time rather than forming populations with fixed $H$.

title: AutoPoly-HE: Autonomous Design of Polynomial Activations for Privacy-Preserving Encrypted Inference
abstract: Privacy-preserving machine learning has become critical for deploying artificial intelligence in sensitive domains such as healthcare, finance, and infrastructure monitoring. Homomorphic encryption (HE) enables secure inference on encrypted data. Despite its advantages, HE is not compatible with nonlinear activation functions found in machine learning models. Existing methods mitigate this problem by manually designing polynomial approximations for these activation functions. However, these functions do not account for the differences in dataset characteristics or model architecture. Furthermore, these functions are also limited to the accuracies of convolutional neural network (CNN) models. In this work, we propose an autonomous framework that selects polynomial activation functions tailored to each dataset and model. Using this framework, we analyze the interdependence between polynomial activation design and model architecture by evaluating several CNN ResNet and Vision Transformer models across multiple datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework generalizes across multiple architectures, including ResNet-18, ResNet-34, ResNet-50, ViT-S/16, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/16. Across all datasets, transformer-based models maintain higher accuracy under polynomial approximation, while convolutional models exhibit increased degradation as task complexity grows. In addition, latency analysis reveals that the proposed CLS token based inference pipeline significantly reduces computational overhead by eliminating depth-dependent operations, shifting the primary cost to encryption and decryption. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method not only adapts polynomial activations across architectures, but also enables efficientencrypted inference through both activation design and pipeline optimization.

title: VerbaRF-Dataset
abstract: The dataset is built from audio recordings of four English textbook volumes, organized by volume and unit. Each unit recording is segmented into individual word segments according to the silent intervals between adjacent pronunciations, after which the word boundaries and labels are manually checked and corrected.The dataset contains 1,350 word classes, 2,673 word segments, and 16,038 RFID samples.

title: Before Meta Muse/Sentinel: What Did Earlier DAS Patent Filings Already Disclose? | An Open Technical Challenge
abstract: Description How much of Meta Muse/Sentinel's AI-agent security workflow was already disclosed in earlier DAS patent filings? This 10-page PDF presents a concise, AI-assisted technical comparison of DAS execution-finality architecture and Meta Muse/Sentinel, publicly announced on 8 September 2026. DAS international filings began in April 2026, with ALF-PCT published on 4 June 2026. DAS I (PCT/IB2026/055615), including Embodiment 85.B2 — Agent Sandbox Egress Finality Gate, was filed on 4 June 2026 and published on 16 July 2026, alongside DAS II and III. DAS IV was published on 23 July 2026. The comparison examines architectural similarities, independent execution authority, sandbox egress, permission withdrawal, escalation and implementation differences. For detailed independent review: Readers are encouraged to download the complete technical disclosure package, including original patent filings, drawings and review instructions: https://zenodo.org/records/23040181 Disclaimer: This is an independent concept-validation exercise, not an allegation of copying or patent infringement. Independent development is entirely possible. AI-assisted analysis may contain errors; readers are requested to verify the original WIPO and Meta sources and draw their own conclusions.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Reinforcement and Mutual Reinforcement Learning for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate candidate answers, evaluate their quality, and use evaluation signals to improve subsequent responses. However, self-evaluation may reinforce a model's own biases and errors, whereas evaluation by other models may introduce evaluator disagreement, capability mismatches, and correlated errors. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Reinforcement and Mutual Reinforcement Learning (ASMR), a multi-LLM learning framework that dynamically switches between independent self-evaluation and cross-model evaluation during iterative training. Given the same input problem, multiple LLMs independently generate candidate answers and assign quality scores to those answers. During self-reinforcement phases, each model evaluates its own candidates and learns from its preferred responses. During mutual-reinforcement phases, models evaluate candidates produced by other models, exchange preference information, and learn from cross-model feedback. A switching controller selects the learning mode according to evaluation disagreement, evaluator reliability, model-specific performance trends, and the availability of informative preference signals. The framework preserves model-specific parameters while permitting controlled exchange of training information. To reduce the risk of self-reinforcing errors, ASMR incorporates score calibration, uncertainty-aware selection, independent verification where available, and safeguards against repeated optimization of unreliable evaluations. We formulate the learning process, define a switching policy, and propose an experimental protocol for comparing adaptive switching with self-reinforcement alone, mutual reinforcement alone, and fixed-proportion hybrid learning. This paper presents a research framework and testable hypotheses rather than empirical findings. Its principal contribution is the explicit formulation and evaluation of adaptive switching between two learning pathways in a multi-LLM system.

title: Which Signal Did the Synthesis Import? Information, Re-presentation and Selection in Synthetic Pretraining, Why 'the Verifier Is Doing the Work' Holds Only Where Correctness Is the Target, and the Controls That Would Assign the Credit
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. The expectation that language models will keep improving after the supply of human text runs out rests on a claim about synthetic data: that a model, or a family of models, can produce training text worth more than the text it was trained on. A competing reading holds that no synthetic-data success is self-generated at all, because every pipeline that works draws on something outside the generating model, most visibly a verifier. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results on synthetic data for pretraining, continued pretraining and mid-training, and argues that both readings are posed at the wrong grain. Read as a conservation law, the imported-signal claim is true and uninformative, since every generator's weights were themselves fitted to human text. Read as a claim about what explains a measured gain, it splits. The paper separates three contributions a synthetic corpus can make - new information, re-presentation of information already in an organic seed, and selection within the generator's own distribution - and four places the signal can come from: the seed text, the generator's prior, a selection signal, and the designer's prompts or grammars. Against that ledger, the best-controlled pretraining gains are mostly re-presentation: they beat repetition of the same corpus, they persist when the generator is small, and summarisation of web pages nearly matches teacher-written textbooks. There is no verifier in those pipelines. The verifier does the work where the target is correctness, in geometry, code and arithmetic. The most self-contained bootstrapping results use held-out human text as the scorer. No located pretraining result shows a gain from self-generation with none of the four sources present, and the pipelines that come closest score below the real-data baseline on factuality. The paper consolidates the reported values, states a credit-assignment protocol, and names the five controls that would settle the open part.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Personalization and Consumer Engagement: Examining the Future of Customer Experience in the Digital Economy
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven personalization has become a transformative innovation in the digital economy, enabling organizations to deliver tailored products, services, and interactions that enhance customer experience and consumer engagement. As AI technologies, including machine learning, predictive analytics, recommendation systems, and chatbots, become increasingly integrated into digital platforms, understanding their influence on consumer behavior is essential for achieving sustainable competitive advantage. This study examined the effects of artificial intelligence-driven personalization on customer experience, customer satisfaction, and consumer engagement in the digital economy. Specifically, it determined the effect of AI-driven personalization on customer experience, examined the influence of customer experience on customer satisfaction, and assessed the combined effects of AI-driven personalization, customer experience, and customer satisfaction on consumer engagement. A mixed methods research design using the convergent parallel approach was adopted. Quantitative data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 400 respondents selected through stratified random sampling, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with 20 purposively selected participants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), whereas qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed that artificial intelligence-driven personalization has a significant positive effect on customer experience, customer experience significantly enhances customer satisfaction, and artificial intelligence-driven personalization, customer experience, and customer satisfaction jointly exert significant positive effects on consumer engagement, with AI-driven personalization emerging as the strongest predictor. Qualitative findings further confirmed that personalized recommendations, predictive services, and intelligent digital interactions improve customer experience, increase satisfaction, and foster sustained consumer engagement. The study concludes that AI-driven personalization is a strategic capability for enhancing customer experience and strengthening long-term consumer engagement in the global digital economy. It recommends that organizations invest in AI-driven personalization technologies, adopt customer-centric digital strategies, integrate AI into customer relationship management systems, and promote ethical AI governance, robust digital infrastructure, and effective consumer data protection to achieve sustainable competitiveness.

title: An academic chatbot with hybrid retrieval and local large language models
abstract: Higher-education institutions devote a substantial share of their staff time to answering queries whose answers are already set out in institutional regulations. This paper presents the design and evaluation of an academic chatbot based on retrieval-augmented generation that lets users query those documents in natural language and receive grounded answers in Spanish. The system combines a structure-aware ingestion pipeline, a hybrid retriever that fuses dense semantic search and lexical search through reciprocal rank fusion, and a locally hosted large language model. A distinguishing goal is data sovereignty: every component runs on institutional hardware, so no data is sent to external services. Quality is evaluated with the RAGAS framework over five regulatory documents: the corpus-wide set attains a global score of 0.90, with faithfulness of 0.97. The acceptance criterion is not met, however, under its conjunctive reading: answer relevancy stays below its threshold across all sets, and p95 latency reaches 6.47 seconds against a 5-second target. Quality further degrades on long, heavily cross-referenced regulations. A contrast questionnaire administered to nineteen users places the perception index at 3.64 out of 5 and exposes a relevant discrepancy: only 57.9% agree that the system does not produce fabricated information, against the faithfulness the automatic judge assigns it.

title: Chaotic slime mould metaheuristic with Chebyshev map for IoT service composition
abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to a proliferation of services offering identical functionalities with heterogeneous capabilities and quality levels. Efficiently composing these IoT services to satisfy user requirements while maintaining system performance under strict Quality of Service constraints, such as energy consumption, remains a challenging combinatorial optimization problem. Metaheuristic algorithms have proven effective in addressing such large-scale optimization tasks. This paper first proposes an energy consumption model for IoT services. It then proposes two novel discrete versions of the Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA) specifically designed for IoT service composition. The first, called Discrete Slime Mould Algorithm (DSMA), adapts SMA to the discrete domain using adaptive fitness-based weights, probabilistic gene copying from the best solution, and an adaptive mutation mechanism. The second, called Chaotic Discrete Slime Mould Algorithm (CDSMA), further integrates Chebyshev chaotic maps for population initialization and weight updating to improve population diversity and accelerate convergence. Experimental results show that CDSMA consistently outperforms DSMA and other classical metaheuristics. CDSMA achieves an optimality rate of 96.33% with a small population size and 99.92% with a moderate population size. Furthermore, extensive experiments over 30 independent runs confirm that both proposed algorithms significantly outperform classical metaheuristics. CDSMA achieves 96.46% (±0.65) optimality, DSMA achieves 93.75% (±0.75), significantly outperforming SMA (84.74%), GWO (82.54%), HHO (82.87%), and WOA (80.15%) with statistical significance (t-test, p < 10-20).

title: Task-Phase-Conditioned Expert Routing Is Not a Reliable Proxy for Quantization Sensitivity in MoE FFN Tensors
abstract: We investigate whether per-layer, per-task-phase (prompt/reasoning/response) expert-routing statistics in a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model can guide layer-wise mixed-precision quantization of routed-expert FFN tensors (down/gate and up). To attain layerwise routing statistics, we build a routing-capture and profiling pipeline for Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B in ik_llama.cpp, derive a composite sensitivity score from routing entropy/decisiveness, coefficient of variation (CV), Jaccard/phase-fragility, and top-1 expert strength, and use coordinate descent to tune a layer allocation that respects a fixed average bits-per-weight budget. Notably, the profiling pipeline is applicable to standard top-k MoE architectures. Across independent experimental conditions (about 4.0 bpw flat, about 2.7 bpw steep, and about 2.7 bpw random allocation as a control), reallocation fails to outperform the uniform baseline within each quality tier. In the flat regime, reallocation is statistically neutral (z about 0.9). For the steep tier, the random reallocation performs within 1 SE of the routing-guided reallocation at the same tier, indicating a structural loss at this quality rung caused by mandatory downgrades and Kullback-Leibler Divergence (KLD) tail injection. evidence.title: Task-Phase-Conditioned Expert Routing Is Not a Reliable Proxy for Quantization Sensitivity in MoE FFN Tensors
evidence.abstract: We investigate whether per-layer, per-task-phase (prompt/reasoning/response) expert-routing statistics in a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model can guide layer-wise mixed-precision quantization of routed-expert FFN tensors (down/gate and up). title: IneqAgent: Agentic Inequality Proving in Lean with Symbolic Computation
abstract: Formal inequality proving requires mathematical reasoning and exact computation, often connected through intermediate lemmas and goal reformulations. We introduce IneqAgent, an agentic framework combining LLM reasoning with symbolic computation for inequality proving in Lean4. Lemma-level Monte Carlo Tree Search coordinates lemma construction, goal reformulation, and symbolic backend selection. Complementary sum-of-squares, Bernstein, and successive difference-substitution backends produce exact certificates for local Lean proof generation. The agent integrates these proofs with LLM-generated steps and uses Lean feedback to construct complete proofs checked against the original theorem statements. On four benchmarks, IneqAgent with DeepSeek-V4-Flash solves 175 of 186 problems (94.09%), achieving the highest overall success rate among the evaluated methods. Across four backbones, it achieves higher success rates at low LLM inference cost thresholds than Direct Agent using the same backbone, with lower mean inference costs over each method's successful runs. We also obtain Lean-verified strengthenings of Dittert's conjecture in dimensions four and five, and certify the Holens--Djokovic $(4,4)$ inequality, implying Merris's conjecture in dimension four.

title: When Occupation-derived Skills Don't Help: On the Limits of Skill-Augmented Career Path Prediction
abstract: Skills are widely assumed to play a central role in career transitions, motivating their use in career path prediction (CPP) systems. In this work, we critically examine whether explicit skill representations provide complementary signal beyond text-based job representations. We evaluate multiple strategies for incorporating skills into CPP models, including score fusion and neural architectures, under two conditions: predicted skills and ground-truth ESCO annotations. Surprisingly, across two benchmark datasets, none of these settings yield substantial improvements over strong text-only baselines. Even when using ground-truth skills, gains remain marginal and inconsistent. Through detailed analysis, we identify key factors underlying this result: high redundancy between textual and skill representations, limited discriminative power of ESCO's taxonomy, and representational collapse in skill embeddings. Furthermore, we find that skill prediction difficulty correlates with overall sample difficulty, limiting the potential for complementary signals. Our findings challenge the common assumption that explicit skill modeling inherently benefits career prediction and suggest that dense text representations already capture most skill-relevant information.

title: Quantum-enhanced phase interrogation of a fiber-optic strain sensor
abstract: Fiber-optic sensors enable high-sensitivity measurements of various physical parameters. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-enhanced interrogation of an all-fiber-optic Fabry-Perot resonator, employing entangled two-photon interference to probe directly strain-induced optical phase shifts. The resonator is interrogated by a narrow-linewidth laser that is frequency-locked to its resonance mode, thereby exploiting the cavity's inherent sensitivity to variations in the fiber length. To access the phase fluctuations transferred to the interrogation field due to external perturbations on the sensor, we implement an in-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer readout. This configuration allows the sensor to operate both with classical coherent light and with entangled photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. Harnessing two-photon entangled states corresponding to an N = 2 NOON state, we experimentally demonstrate a reduction of the measurement noise below the standard quantum limit. These results provide clear evidence of the quantum advantage in enhancing fiber-optic sensors under practical constraints on optical power.

title: Covariance Intersection for Robust Sensor Fusion in Anti-drone Defense System
abstract: In this study, we aim to establish a radar sensor-based defense system against the threat of suicide drones, which are not limited to attacks on personnel but can also neutralize critical friendly assets, including armored vehicles. Since drone tracking relies heavily on sensor performance, sensor fusion is employed to prepare for situations in which sensor performance is degraded, such as jamming attacks or sensor failures. First, an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) is used to estimate the position of an enemy drone in X, Y, and Z coordinates based on range, elevation, and azimuth measurements from radar sensors. The position estimation performance is further improved through sensor fusion using the Covariance Intersection (CI) method. To address sensor degradation, an Adaptive Kalman Filter (AKF), which updates the R matrix of the UKF, and a Fault Detection and Isolation (FDI) algorithm are applied to suppress the influence of degraded sensors. Simulations are conducted under assumed sensor-degradation scenarios, such as Noise Modulation Jamming and Range Deception Jamming, affecting a specific sensor. The results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains excellent position-estimation performance even under such conditions and enables interception of enemy drones using the Proportional Navigation Guidance (PNG) algorithm.

title: SHAP-guided IBRB reproducibility materials
abstract: Code and computational records accompanying A hybrid interpretable risk assessment method for lung cancer integrating SHAP with a supervised interval belief rule base. The package contains the analysis, reconstruction, retraining and acquisition code together with the frozen configurations, evaluation split membership, fitted models, per-fold predictions, statistical summaries and the numerical values underlying the figures and tables. The original 5,000-record benchmark uses two repetitions of stratified five-fold evaluation, with SHAP and IBRB sharing a designated 1,000-record fitting subset of the outer training pool. The independent NLST analysis uses 6,996 baseline-CT patients (5,200 development, 1,796 confirmation). Project-authored code is licensed under MIT. Author-created figures, explanatory text and aggregate analytical summaries are licensed under CC BY 4.0. The NLST public clinical subset is redistributed under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution and modification notices in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Source attribution, licensing and the documented changes for each dataset are recorded in DATA_AVAILABILITY.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Numerical reconstruction is reproducible from the archived materials; the frozen-model check restores 10 original-benchmark and 11 NLST primary models and verifies 220 original-benchmark model/fold conditions and nine NLST confirmation conditions.

title: Conformal prediction for byte-level CPS traffic classification under adversarial attacks
abstract: AI-driven traffic classification is increasingly used in networked cyber–physical systems (CPS) (e.g., smart grids) to enable monitoring from packet-byte representations, without relying on protocol-specific parsing. However, recent work shows that learning-based traffic classifiers can be vulnerable to adaptive adversarial manipulation of observed packet bytes, leading to severe degradation and brittle decisioning at runtime. In this paper, we propose a security-oriented traffic classification framework that integrates adversarial robustness with calibrated uncertainty quantification for CPS networks. Our approach employs a byte-level representation that requires no protocol-specific feature engineering, evaluates robustness under adaptive Carlini–Wagner attacks, and incorporates conformal prediction to provide statistical risk control on predictions during inference. Across multiple CPS traffic datasets, we show that adversarial perturbations substantially reduce classification performance, while adversarial retraining improves robustness. Further, conformal prediction exposes low-confidence regimes and supports reliable operational handling of suspicious or adversarial traffic via selective prediction (accept/reject) with coverage guarantees.

title: Leveraging High-Frequency Postoperative ICU Arterial Blood Pressure Data from Electronic Health Records for Research: A Brief Report
abstract: Postoperative blood pressure fluctuations after cardiac surgery are highly clinically relevant, yet analyzing high-frequency arterial pressure data remains challenging. In this study, we introduce a novel methodology for processing minute-by-minute postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) arterial pressure data. The pipeline implements a series of systematic data-cleaning steps to resolve artifacts and ensure physiological plausibility, and deploys a multi-stage imputation framework to address missing intervals. Our approach constructs longitudinal blood pressure profiles that quantify the time spent within predefined blood pressure ranges, minimizing assumptions and enhancing data utility for research. We detail a rigorous and reusable workflow for data extraction, cleaning, and imputation, which may address limitations of previous methods and offer a framework to build a robust exposure metric for future research utilizing postoperative arterial pressure data.

title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions with Bounded Input Degree
abstract: We prove the weak composition-independence conjectures of Kohn, Marchetti, Massarenti and Mella. The proof uses deformations of rational curves and a single kernel of the linearized equation. Riemann-Roch gives a contradiction from tangent fields with controlled poles. By settling these conjectures, we prove that a neural network with a general polynomial activation function of sufficiently large degree is identifiable.

title: FreeSBee: A Constant-Time Compilation Pipeline
abstract: Constant-time execution is an important security property, especially for IoT devices, that prevents the leakage of sensitive information over timing side-channels. However, achieving constant-time execution is very hard when going down to the cycle level, at least on realistic devices. A lot of research is concerned with producing tools that either determine whether code is constant-time or that ensure it is compiled into a constant-time binary, with various degrees of accuracy. In this work, we present and evaluate a full workflow for hardening against timing side-channels during compilation. It starts with taint analysis to determine the code locations that depend on sensitive information. These are then the object of automated control-flow transformations inside the compiler to seal possible timing side-channels. We evaluate our workflow in detail on a realistic application running on a RISC-V core using both static timing analysis and statistical methods. Even though we do not reach cycle-accurate constant-time execution, our statistical results suggest that our hardened binary is safe against timing attacks.

title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Rényi Entropies Estimation
abstract: Entropy estimation of discrete probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistical inference and quantum property estimation. In this paper, we study the problem of estimating Rényi entropy $H_α(\mathbf{p})$ for any distribution $\mathbf{p} = (p_i)_{i=1}^n$ given its purified quantum query-access. For non-integer $α> 1$, our algorithm estimates $H_α(\mathbf{p})$ to within additive error $ε$ using only $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{\max\{1/2,1-1/α\}}/ε\big)$ queries, which improves the best known upper bound for dependence on both $n$ and $1/ε$. For $0<α<1$, our algorithm has query complexity $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{1/(2α)}/ε^{\max\{1,1/(2α)\}}\big)$, which improves the dependence on $1/ε$ of the current best upper bound without incresing its $n$ dependence. Our approach adapts the multi-level estimation framework to relative approximation of the power sums and leverage binary search to remove the requirement of prior knowledge of them. We also strengthen the precision-dependent lower bound to $Ω\big(1/ε^{\max\{1,1/(2α)\}}\big)$ for $0<α<1$, which identifies the optimal precision dependence of our algorithm.

title: BluePixel: Toward Native 4K Agentic Image Editing
abstract: Instruction-driven image editing has reached native 4K, yet how such editors are trained remains undisclosed, and pretraining one from scratch is beyond most teams. The task itself compounds the difficulty: a single end-to-end editor cannot make precise parametric adjustments, match specialized experts, or interpret the vague instructions users actually write. We argue that 4K editing is a system problem rather than a single-model problem, and present BluePixel, which couples a native-4K editing model with an agent harness; the complete training recipe is disclosed in this paper. The model makes 4K training practical: it turns a 1K-pretrained editor into a native-4K one through progressive VAE adaptation that keeps 4K training as affordable as 1K, absorbs a long tail of vertical editing skills through continual learning, and refines the aesthetic-fidelity trade-off with reinforcement learning. Distillation via source-anchored target projection (SATP) then compresses 50 denoising steps to 4, completing a 4K edit in 8.7 s on a single Kunlunxin P800 XPU while preserving task success rate and background consistency. The harness, BluePixel Agent, makes editing controllable: it decomposes user instructions into specialist and general operations, verifies every result with the same reward model that guided training, and retries within bounded attempts. On VINS-4KEval++ (3,305 native-4K cases), BluePixel ranks second among seven models, behind only GPT Image 2 in non-edited-region consistency.

title: Data from: Spectroscopy using dipole-phonon quantum logic
abstract: *Data embargoed until publication of related article, or up to no more than 1 year from data upload.* Raw photon counts and processed shot records of the four dipole-phonon quantum logic (DPQL) datasets analysed in the paper "Spectroscopy using dipole-phonon quantum logic" (L. Qi, E. C. Reed, D. Wang, B. Yu, K. R. Brown), together with the code that reproduces the processed records from the raw counts. A single CaO+ molecular ion (or, for the control, CaOH+) was co-trapped with a Ca+ ion in a room-temperature segmented blade Paul trap at the Duke Quantum Center. In each experiment the frequency of the axial out-of-phase motional mode was ramped adiabatically through the predicted ground-state Omega-doublet resonance of CaO+, and the resulting phonon was mapped onto the Ca+ ion with a 729 nm red-sideband pulse and read out by state-dependent fluorescence. Four datasets were recorded: CaO+ with the ramp 2pi x [492, 412] kHz (1,568,521 experiments kept), the CaOH+ control over the same range (1,647,755), and CaO+ with the ramps 2pi x [454, 370] kHz (1,618,369) and 2pi x [534, 454] kHz (1,388,915). Data were collected September-October 2025 and April 2026. Raw files are plain-text photomultiplier counts: for each experiment, the Ca+ detection count after the red-sideband pulse and a post-selection count after an 854 nm quench pulse, in blocks of 10,000 experiments each followed by a 40-point tickle scan used as the dark-ion mass check. Processed files mark each kept experiment as dark (1, shelving event) or bright (0), using a detection threshold of 2 counts and keeping only experiments whose post-selection count is at least 3. processing_log.csv lists which raw blocks built each processed file; code/process_raw.py (Python, numpy) rebuilds every processed file and the four analysis streams from the raw counts and checks that they match the deposited files exactly. MANIFEST.csv gives SHA-256 checksums of all files. See README.txt for the folder layout, file formats and the three 10,000-experiment blocks excluded because the 729 nm laser lost lock.

title: HR7/PFA — 90-Day Prospective Frozen-Case Validation 1-AI Systems-Report
abstract: Abstract This report presents the completed 90-day (M3) prospective validation of ten previously frozen assessments conducted under the HR7 Historical Reference Framework and Predictive Feasibility Assessment (PFA). The original assessments were registered on 8 July 2026 and remained unchanged throughout the observation period ending on 6 October 2026. The study covers ten AI systems: GPT-4o, Google Gemini, Meta Llama 3, Microsoft Copilot, Amazon Bedrock, Tesla Autopilot, Waymo Driverless System, IBM watsonx, Amazon Recommendation Engine, and NVIDIA NeMo. Recorded validation results: M1 (30 days): 10 SUPPORTED M2 (60 days): 10 SUPPORTED (reconstructed internal aggregate summary; complete original M2 documentation not independently recovered) M3 (90 days): 10 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED No decisive contradiction of the original frozen classifications was established within the reviewed evidence. The M3 assessment applied stricter evidentiary scrutiny than M1 and M2, particularly concerning independent operational measurements, product-specific attribution, deployment maturity, and falsifiability. Consequently, the validation categories across the three checkpoints are not directly comparable as quantitative measures of predictive accuracy. The principal finding is that HR7/PFA maintained attention on relevant technological and operational deployment constraints during the observation period. However, the available evidence does not establish statistically validated forecasting accuracy or predictive superiority over simpler baseline methods. This report contains the ten individual case assessments, the cross-case evidence synthesis, methodological limitations, and the final 90-day scientific conclusion. Original frozen T0 publication:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21268618 Observation period: 8 July–6 October 2026 Author: Jos Aben, Independent Researcher

The M3 assessment applied stricter evidentiary scrutiny than M1 and M2, particularly concerning independent operational measurements, product-specific attribution, deployment maturity, and falsifiability. This report contains the ten individual case assessments, the cross-case evidence synthesis, methodological limitations, and the final 90-day scientific conclusion. title: Adaptive Parallel-World Self-Rewarding and Cross-Model Mutual Rewarding for Large Language Models
abstract: Reward generation is a central component of reinforcement learning, preference optimization, and self-improvement in large language models (LLMs). Existing approaches have demonstrated that an LLM can evaluate its own outputs and use the resulting judgments to improve its behavior. However, self-rewarding systems may suffer from self-evaluation bias, limited evaluative diversity, and the accumulation of errors across iterative optimization. Cross-model evaluation can introduce additional perspectives, but relying exclusively on external evaluators may increase computational costs and create new dependencies. This paper proposes Adaptive Parallel-World Self-Rewarding and Cross-Model Mutual Rewarding (APSMR), a unified framework that dynamically coordinates self-rewarding and mutual rewarding across multiple LLMs and multiple evaluative branches of the same underlying model. In APSMR, a parallel world is defined as an independently configured evaluative branch derived from the same underlying model, with each branch assigned a potentially different reward orientation, evaluation rubric, reasoning strategy, or task perspective. The framework distinguishes intra-model parallel-world self-rewarding from inter-branch mutual rewarding and cross-model mutual rewarding. An adaptive controller selects among these modes according to estimated reward reliability, disagreement, uncertainty, task characteristics, computational cost, and observed feedback quality. A reliability-aware reward aggregation mechanism combines available judgments while accounting for evaluator dependence and calibration. The resulting rewards can support candidate selection, preference-pair construction, supervised refinement, or reinforcement-learning-based policy optimization. This paper formalizes the framework, presents its operational algorithm, proposes a multi-stage evaluation protocol, and identifies testable research hypotheses. The framework is intended to reduce dependence on a single evaluation pathway rather than assume that mutual rewarding is always superior to self-rewarding. Because APSMR is a proposed method, its comparative effectiveness remains an empirical question. The paper provides a reproducible experimental blueprint for evaluating reward accuracy, downstream task performance, robustness, calibration, computational efficiency, and resistance to reward manipulation.

title: A Data-Driven Framework for Music Aesthetic Education Content Optimization
abstract: To address the problems of homogenized content, delayed feedback, and insufficient alignment between teaching content and student interests in music aesthetic education, this study presents a data-driven framework for curriculum content optimization. The framework integrates multi-source student data and applies K-means clustering to build student personas, while using a content-matching mechanism and sentiment analysis to support adaptive recommendations and feedback optimization. A four-week comparative teaching experiment involving 150 undergraduate students from a cooperating university demonstrates that the proposed framework can improve student satisfaction and engagement compared with traditional teaching approaches. The study also discusses its adaptability across different educational contexts and offers a practical approach to personalized, intelligent development of music aesthetic education.

title: Design and optimization of a corpus-based intelligent support system for English teaching
abstract: This article focuses on the design and algorithm optimization of an English language teaching (ELT) intelligent assistance system based on corpus. The system relies on an English corpus containing multiple sources of text such as news, academic papers, and literary works, with a total of over 5 million words. It is designed for middle school English teachers and students, and includes modules for teaching resource push, intelligent Q&A, and learning evaluation. The system can dynamically push personalized learning content based on learner profiles and learning behavior data, and provide answers and feedback through natural language interaction. Algorithmically, a deep learning model was constructed that integrates recurrent neural network (RNN), long-term and short-term memory network (LSTM), and attention mechanism. The hyperparameters were optimized through random search and grid search, and multiple layers of LSTM and skip connections were introduced. A one semester experiment was conducted on two parallel classes in the first grade of a certain middle school. The experimental group used the system and optimization algorithm, while the control group used traditional teaching. The results showed that the average post test English score of the experimental group (82.3) was higher than that of the control group (76.8), and both the learning interest score (3.8 vs. 3.2) and the self-directed learning ability score (3.6 vs. 3.0) improved. The prediction accuracy of the system for vocabulary, grammar, and reading problems is 85%, 82%, and 78%, respectively, and the response time meets the requirements of real-time learning.
